subject: Proposal: FounderLab cohort promo structure and conversion path
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan@founderslab.co>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@founderslab.co
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: FounderLab cohort — promo credits & conversion question

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We run a 12-week FounderLab cohort starting Oct 4 and want to provide participants with a sandbox stipend. Historically we've done $10k credits per team, but our finance team asked whether Redwood can: (1) apply a cohort-level promo pool rather than per-team credits, and (2) offer a conversion credit if a cohort team converts to a paid commitment within 120 days.

Key asks:
- Can we pool promo credits (one bucket for the cohort) that teams draw from?
- Is there precedent for a conversion credit (apply X% of unused promo to first invoice if they commit)?
- Are there guardrails for abuse (multiple accounts, overages)?

Attached is a rough milestone spreadsheet for the cohort (founderslab-milestones.xlsx). Procurement is CC'd — they will handle contracting and tax forms.

Appreciate any options you can share by early next week; we need to finalize sponsor funding next Monday.

Best,
Megan
Megan Li
Program Director, FounderLab
megan@founderslab.co
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan@founderslab.co>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FounderLab cohort — promo credits & conversion question

Hi Megan — great to hear the demo landed well.

Short answers up front: yes on a pooled promo bucket; yes on a conversion credit structure; and we can implement guardrails. A few clarifying points so I give you concrete numbers:

1) Pooled promo bucket model: we can issue a cohort-level credit (account-level promo) that participants draw from. Admins (you or procurement) would have a single code and we can track token consumption per participant for reporting. This avoids over-provisioning and simplifies reconciliation.

2) Conversion credit: we typically apply a conversion credit as a fixed dollar credit or percentage of a paid commitment. Example we often use: "conversion credit = 25% of unused promo (capped at $5k per team) applied toward first invoice if customer signs a 12-month Reserved/Dedicated commitment within 90–120 days." We can tailor the cap and window.

3) Abuse guardrails: we enforce unique billing contacts, limit of one promo redemption per legal entity, and monitor for token bursts with automated flagging. For cohorts where teams are companies (not individuals), this works cleanly.

Suggested promo structure for FounderLab (proposal):
- Cohort bucket: $150,000 promo credits shared across cohort (estimate based on ~15 teams at $10k each).
- Ramp rules: promotional credits burn at standard hosted rate; overages billed to team card after promo exhaustion unless you want a hard cap.
- Conversion offer: if a team converts to a 12-month Reserved capacity or Annual commitment within 120 days, we apply a credit equal to 30% of their unused portion of the cohort promo, capped at $7,500 per team.
- Contracting: cohort admin signs a short addendum; participants sign an acknowledgement to prevent duplicate accounts.

I'll loop finance and ops to surface constraints (billing caps, tax). Attached is a draft term sheet (redwood-promo-term-sheet.pdf) — it's intentionally conservative.

If that aligns, I can ask Ben (finance) and Grace (ops) to scope billing flows and quick anti-abuse checks. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Monday.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FounderLab cohort — promo credits & conversion question

Markus — looping in ops and finance notes. Quick items from my side:

- Promo accounting: a $150k cohort bucket is fine but we need to classify as a marketing promotion with a specific AR recognition path. If FoundersLab requires an invoice to the cohort admin (sponsor), we need PO/contract details up front.
- Cap & overage: propose we protect Redwood by enforcing a per-team overage cap of $12k (after which the admin is notified and teams must add billing). We can also set alerts at 75%/90% burn.
- Conversion credit math: 30% of unused promo capped at $7.5k per team is okay; finance prefers a 90-day conversion window for revenue recognition alignment, but can extend to 120 days if FoundersLab provides sponsor approval.
- Legal/Procurement: procurement@founderslab.co will likely ask for an MSA addendum. We can fast-track with a CRO-approved short addendum.

I attached a quick template term-sheet and the milestone workbook comments. If FoundersLab is comfortable with sponsor invoicing and the cap rules, finance can sign off by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-promo-term-sheet.pdf (see section 3 for conversion credit details)
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan@founderslab.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, procurement@founderslab.co
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FounderLab cohort — promo credits & conversion question

Megan — thanks for the patience. After looping finance and ops, here's a concrete, sponsor-friendly proposal for FounderLab to finalize sponsor funding: 

Proposal (final):
- Cohort promo bucket: $150,000 applied as a single promo code. FounderLab (sponsor) will receive an invoice for the promo bucket and act as the billing admin.
- Team entitlement: teams draw from the cohort pool. We will limit redemptions to one legal entity per team; teams must register with their company email.
- Overages & caps: teams incur overages billed to the team card after promo exhaustion. Redwood will set automated alerts at 75% and 90% bucket burn and a hard safety cap per team at $12k.
- Conversion credit: if a team signs a 12‑month Reserved/Dedicated commitment within 120 days, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 30% of that team's unused promo value (capped at $7,500). Admin provides a list of converted teams and signed contracts to redeem.
- Timeline & docs: we will provide a short addendum for the sponsor PO and a simple participant acknowledgement. Term sheet and milestone workbook attached.

Next steps:
1) Megan — confirm sponsor is comfortable with invoice-for-promo model and the $150k total.
2) Procurement — if OK, please return PO by Fri 2026-09-10.
3) Redwood — we'll provision the promo code and set dashboard reporting for cohort admin.

If these terms work, I will send the doc for signature (DocuSign link included) and we can ramp before Oct 4.

Regards,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
